# ISSUE-311 plan

Expose the installed Maven/Gradle runtime closure only inside the existing Linux harness-tools restore boundary. This resolves the real188 dogfood blocker without changing #188 adapters. This phase produces PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md only.

## Dimensions and gates

Approved dimensions: small / known / sensitive; approved execution profile: sensitive. Budget: 16 hours including planning, implementation and validation. A bounded installed-layout resolver and fixtures should fit one cycle; arbitrary distribution support would not. Require an independent security/design review of the closure rules and adversarial coverage, then the human plan approval required by WORKUNIT.md, before implementation. Reviewers must verify these proposals against approved inputs; this document grants no authority or approval.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:43` (`restoreFlags`) binds /usr/bin and /usr/lib plus fixed compatibility paths, but neither /usr/share nor /etc/alternatives. Launchers pointing there cannot resolve their installed runtime with those mounts alone.
- `internal/sandbox/restore.go:21` defines RestoreRequest as coordinator input, not candidate configuration. `:45` checks capability without payload execution; `:239` strips argv for that check. Preserve the generic canary's independence from installed Maven/Gradle availability.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go:22` runs descriptor closure, filesystem/network/broker canaries and READY/GO acknowledgement before payload execution; `:110` supplies a fixed payload environment including generated public JVM trust. Preserve this protocol and resource limits (`restore_linux.go:23`).
- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:64,196,286,349` already cover launcher flags, real boundary isolation, cleanup and source special files. `restore_test.go:260` covers invalid inputs; `restore_protocol_test.go` covers the registry broker transport.
- `internal/sandbox/executor_test.go:89` tests ordinary ToolExecutor isolation. Its real-boundary tests require SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1; restore mount changes must never propagate into that executor.
- `Makefile` defines make fmt and make check (lint, race tests, changelog check). The compiled policy additionally requires go build ./..., go vet ./..., go tool staticcheck ./..., and go test ./....
- Proposed new files below are absent in this supplied snapshot (filesystem existence checks). Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails); developer must confirm absence at the approved base before creating them. If present there, treat them as modifications and reconcile before work.

## What we're assuming

- Operator evidence reports /usr/bin/mvn and gradle resolving into /usr/share installations, Java under /usr/lib through alternatives, and Maven libraries linking into /usr/share/java. These host-specific facts are not independently verified here. Deterministic fixtures will check those shapes; operator live checks will check the actual installation.
- A fixed manifest for the reported system-installed layouts is sufficient. Cheapest check: compare the fixture manifest with operator-provided launcher/library topology during independent review. Do not support arbitrary package managers, home installations or repository wrappers.
- Host installation files are coordinator-trusted only after ownership, ancestor permissions, type and canonical-path checks. A pathname under /usr alone is insufficient evidence of trust.

## Open questions

- Which exact launcher-support metadata and library subdirectories are necessary for the supported layouts? Step 1 fixes an explicit manifest from installed launcher conventions, then fixtures test every entry. Unknown layouts return an actionable unsupported-layout error; they do not expand allowed roots.
- Will Maven 3.9 / Gradle 4.4 run with Java 25 under the existing finite limits? Operator PR review checks this separately. JVM compatibility or memory failures do not justify increasing limits, broad mounts, or blocking implementation on an unavailable host. Record incompatibilities for maintainer disposition.
- Approved-base absence of new files cannot be proven without Git metadata in this snapshot. Confirm at implementation checkout before creating those files.

## Design and exact touchpoints

Modify `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go` (`restoreCommand`, `restoreFlags`) to prepare validated runtime inputs before spawning Bubblewrap and add only narrow read-only staged mounts/validated namespace aliases. Keep the platform-neutral request API, non-Linux failure path and check-only behavior unchanged. Existing control-directory ownership/lifetime remains responsible for staging cleanup; no new public runtime-path option.

Create, subject to approved-base absence verification:

- `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go`: unexported `resolveRestoreRuntime`, `stageRestoreRuntime`, runtime manifest/mount types and bounded safe traversal helpers. Use existing `internal/safefs` APIs for root-bound reads and exclusive atomic staged writes; no new filesystem framework.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux_test.go`: resolver/staging table fixtures, mount assertions and adversarial tests.
- `changes/unreleased/311.md`: concise user-facing description of narrow trusted installed-runtime support.

Modify `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go`: extend flags assertions and add actual fixture launches. Modify `internal/sandbox/executor_test.go` only to add an unconditional ordinary-executor mount-plan regression if existing coverage cannot assert absence of the added runtime paths. No adapter, registry policy, helper, broker, native Codex, OCI, protected-file or documentation expansion.

### Runtime authority and closure

1. Select only fixed trusted launchers /usr/bin/mvn or /usr/bin/gradle when the coordinator payload's executable is that launcher (or its independently resolved canonical equivalent). Generic payloads and check-only nil argv add no runtime mounts. Never discover executables through PATH, JAVA_HOME, MAVEN_HOME, GRADLE_HOME, cwd, wrappers, build files, repository manifests, host caches or user configuration. Do not execute launchers, package managers, ldd or build code on the host to discover dependencies.
2. Define code-owned layout manifests for /usr/share/maven and /usr/share/gradle: exact launcher/support files, fixed boot/lib and Gradle lib/plugins JAR enumeration rules. Resolve /usr/bin/java through the specific /etc/alternatives/java link to its validated /usr/lib JVM target. Add only necessary individual aliases; never mount /etc/alternatives itself. Keep existing /usr/lib visibility unchanged. No broad /usr/share, /etc, home, cache or installation-tree directory binds.
3. Enumerate only the supported manifest's library entries, recursively following symlinks with hop/count/byte/depth bounds and cycle detection. Permit a library cross-link into /usr/share/java only for an individually validated regular JAR required by that manifest, including further versioned JAR links. This is a narrow typed cross-root edge, not permission to follow any path under /usr/share. Recreate necessary aliases within the staged namespace so launcher canonicalization/classpaths still work. Reject dangling links, path traversal, unexpected external targets, special files, mount destination collisions and broad parent destinations.
4. Validate every path component and symlink hop, not only the final target. Production inputs and ancestors must have trusted system ownership and must not be group/world writable. Reject paths into source/repository, /cache, host temp, user homes, credentials, settings.xml, gradle.properties, init scripts, private keys or unrelated /etc configuration, including when reached through an otherwise allowed JAR name. Do not import installation conf directories. Only explicitly reviewed public launcher metadata (for example Maven classworlds configuration) may be included; unknown configuration requirements fail closed. A JAR filename alone is not sufficient authority.
5. Pin traversal to trusted roots and copy validated regular files into a private control/runtime snapshot using safefs; preserve necessary read/execute modes without privilege bits. Build aliases only from validated edges, never copy uncontrolled symlinks into a mounted directory. Copy from the validated open handle, revalidate metadata/identity where required and fail on concurrent replacement or mutation; never validate then bind a mutable host pathname. Stage bounded directory contents before constructing a deterministic sorted mount list. Mount selected staged files/subtrees read-only at exact runtime destinations, with only empty parent directories as needed.
6. Complete validation/staging before Bubblewrap or payload launch. Missing executable/library, unsupported layout, unsafe input or exhausted traversal budget produces a bounded error naming runtime/category and remediation (install a supported system layout); do not echo contents, host credentials or repository-controlled diagnostic text. Failed preparation leaves no result and removes staging. Installed client absence must not fail generic restore preflight or ordinary execution.

Trusted installation metadata determines what runtime bytes enter the boundary. Repository pom.xml/build.gradle/settings.gradle and plugins remain untrusted executable build code: they execute only after existing canaries inside the same isolated restore boundary. They cannot enlarge the runtime closure or broker authority.

## Implementation sequence

1. Independent reviewer scrutinizes the fixed manifest, cross-root JAR edges, ownership checks, pinned snapshot strategy and proposed negative tests; resolve findings in these artifacts. Obtain exact-content human plan approval through the normal coordinator workflow before implementation.
2. Confirm base/new-file status; implement bounded resolver/stager with a package-private fixture filesystem seam. Production roots/manifests remain fixed; tests cannot expose a public configurable host-root feature. Add unconditional table-driven tests first, including concurrent replacement and credential exclusion.
3. Integrate runtime preparation in the Linux launcher using the existing private control directory, preserving argv literal handling and all existing flags. Extend flag and cleanup tests. Do not require both tools installed when requesting one; do not inspect either for nil/generic argv.
4. Add deterministic installed-layout boundary fixtures for both tools with chained /usr/share/java links and Java-alternatives topology. Use synthetic executable/runtime markers to prove dependency access and completion inside Bubblewrap, not an installed JVM/client. Keep test-only roots confined to package-private fixture wiring that calls the same production validator and mount renderer. Fixture ownership trust may be injected only privately; production trust policy stays fixed.
5. Add negative tests and ordinary-executor non-widening assertions; add the changelog fragment. Run focused and required checks. Prepare operator review checklist for installed clients without turning those checks into capability/startup gates.

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: `restore_linux.go:27,43` (launcher/flags), `restore.go:239,243` (check-only and launcher call; preserve API), `restore_helper.go:22,110` (protocol/environment; preserve unchanged). New private resolver/stager symbols are described above.
- Extend `restore_linux_test.go:32,48,64,196,286` fixtures/capability/flags/isolation/cleanup; preserve `restore_linux_test.go:96` helper startup and `restore_test.go:202,260,440` snapshot/input/capability coverage. Reuse broker fixtures in `restore_protocol_test.go:51` unchanged.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestoreRuntime' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestore' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestToolExecutor.*Runtime' -count=1`; `SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestToolExecutorBoundary$' -count=1` on a namespace-capable Linux runner. Detailed mappings and mandatory commands are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: read active contract, compiled policy, project/architecture/conventions and /swarm-plan command; inspected actual mounts and helper environment/protocol; searched restoreCommand/restoreFlags/RestoreRequest/RestoreBoundary call sites and existing tests; checked proposed file absence in snapshot. No installed-client compatibility or test-pass claim is made by this planning phase.
- Reopen plan if support needs broader directories/configuration, repository-selected dependencies, changed broker/network/resource/helper behavior, adapter work, a public path-selection API, or a filesystem facility unavailable in safefs. Do not silently widen scope. Unavailable live hosts are review gaps, not implementation startup gates.
- **What this change breaks:** `restore_linux_test.go:64` directly asserts restoreFlags contents: extend while preserving isolation assertions. `restore_linux_test.go:80,313` directly calls restoreCommand: preserve signatures and missing-bwrap behavior. `restore.go:243` and `restore_other.go:11` depend on the common launcher signature: preserve unchanged. `restore_helper.go:110` depends on fixed executable paths/environment: recreate only validated aliases and preserve environment unchanged. `executor_test.go:89` and toolchain mount tests depend on ordinary isolation: preserve ordinary mounts unchanged, add a regression. Existing restore broker/protocol/helper/startup tests remain unchanged except fixture reuse. No docs/templates/adapter callers require updates; repository search found launcher symbols confined to restore files. Add only the required changelog fragment.

## Operator guidance

> Dogfood real188 blocker. Existingrestorefixedmounts omit /usr/share and /etc/alternatives; /usr/bin/mvn andgradle symlink toshare installationtrees; Java resolvesunderusr/lib but Maven JARs maysymlink other /usr/share/java libraries. Plan narrow trusted readonly runtimeclosure, no broadshare/etc/home/cachemounts, no repositoryselectedpaths orhostexecution. Distinguish fixedtrusted toolmetadata from untrustedrepo buildcode; reject symlinkescape/specialfiles/credential exposure. Preserve broker/network/resources/helpercanary. Deterministic fixtures acceptance; installed Maven3.9/Gradle4.4/Java25 live checks operatorreview not startupgate. Independently review design then humanapproval before implementation. PLAN/TEST_PLAN only; no changes to188adapter work.
